quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer affects you less than wine.
Wine affects you less than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you the most.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol harms your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream matters.

questions.question: Is it against the law to drive at night using only parking lights?
questions.explanation: You cannot drive at night using only parking lights. You must use your headlights when driving in the dark.

questions.question: When is it legal to pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
Even if you have to drive off the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right of a vehicle turning left or waiting to turn left if there is an available passing lane. You may also pass on the right on a multi-lane road with two or more lanes in your direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren, no matter which direction it is going. Move to the right side of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: Blind spots around a truck or bus.
A road with restrictions on stereo volume.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in the back, and in the front. Cars cannot be seen in these spots. These blind spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: You are waiting at a stop sign. The vehicles ahead pass through the intersection. If there is no other traffic, can you proceed without stopping again?

options.text: Yes, you may go through without stopping.
No, you must stop again at the stop sign before proceeding.
Yes, you may slowly roll past the stop sign.
Yes, you may follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, you must stop again at the stop sign before proceeding.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not skip this step, even if other cars are behind you.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement mean?

options.text: Drivers may make the movement shown by the arrow if they choose.
Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers must always stop before making the movement shown by the arrow.
Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow painted on the pavement tells drivers in that lane to make the movement the arrow shows. Follow any traffic signs or signals before moving in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass if you are in the lane next to the broken line.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a pedestrian crossing. Watch for people in the crosswalk. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: How should you prepare for anything ahead on the road?

options.text: Scan the whole road and roadsides constantly.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan the whole road and roadsides constantly.
questions.explanation: Finding and spotting problems before you reach them is the key to handling dangerous situations. Look ahead, but also scan the sides of the road. Do not just stare at the center.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Slow down by releasing the gas pedal before using the brakes.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to stop in time. When stopping, release the gas pedal first to slow down. Then press the brake pedal firmly to stop smoothly and turn on your brake lights.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks and obey all signs and signals. Trains, cars, and bicyclists all share the road.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:
questions.explanation: A red light means stop before entering the intersection. Stop at the stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: Orange signs are:
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are diamond-shaped and orange with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers that people are working on or near the highway.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign:

options.text: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs tell you a train might be coming. Obey all railroad signs and never drive around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during the day only.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines show traffic moving in opposite directions. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a roundabout is coming. Enter slowly and yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When driving in fog:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
You can drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead. Use low beams in fog and rain. High beams reflect light back into your eyes and make it harder to see.

questions.question: To avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots:

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: You can drive across a dashed white line:

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross dashed lines to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down when a driver behind you wants to pass. This gives them more space in front of your car to complete the pass safely and quickly.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Go through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light is used at dangerous intersections. Always treat it like a stop sign.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: The legal maximum or minimum speed you can drive.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The legal maximum or minimum speed you can drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the legal maximum or minimum speed allowed on that road. These limits apply in ideal conditions. You must slow down when weather or road conditions are poor.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash through it means something is prohibited. This sign means you cannot make U-turns where it is posted.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, you should:
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who might not see you. If another driver is about to hit you, honk your horn to alert them.

questions.question: You do not have to yield to pedestrians if they are crossing against the traffic light.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing against the light. Pedestrians may not see the light correctly and step into traffic.

questions.question: You should signal ____ feet before you start to turn.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. This tells other drivers what you plan to do. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: You find a problem with your vehicle that could affect safety. You should:

options.text: Fix it when you have money.

questions.explanation: Fix any safety problems with your vehicle as soon as possible. Do not drive the vehicle until the problem is fixed.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, or flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.

questions.explanation: Always yield to emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so wait until the road is clear before you move.

questions.question: Can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or a train whistle. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.explanation: Stop signs are eight-sided. All eight-sided signs tell drivers to stop completely before going forward.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they must do. It means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only on the left and right sides.

questions.explanation: Keep space all around your vehicle so you can react to dangers. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: When must you stop at an intersection?

options.text: When you see a flashing red light.
When you see a steady yellow light.
When you see a yellow arrow.
When you see a flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Which statement is true about wet roads?

options.text: At higher speeds, your tires grip the road less.
Good tires are not affected by water.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Slower speeds make roads more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: At higher speeds, your tires grip the road less.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on wet roads, the less your tires can grip the road. If you go too fast, your tires may lose contact with the road and you will hydroplane, or slide on a layer of water.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up as fast as possible.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. But first, let any traffic and pedestrians in the intersection go ahead of you.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to it.
Let it share only half a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle deserves a full lane, just like any other vehicle. Even if there seems to be room to share, motorcycles need space to move safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right.
